newsitem.title: UK: Cellular firms urged to act on "churn epidemic".
newsitem.headline: Cellular firms urged to act on "churn epidemic".

text.p: Mobile telephone companies should switch their attention to retaining customers rather than simply adding new subscribers, a study by management group Andersen Consulting said on Monday.

"Companies need to get their customer retention figures up and stop focusing on customer numbers rather than customer value," said Richard Siber, associate partner in Andersen Consulting's wireless arm.
"It's not about signing up as many customers as you can anymore. Operators need to be more discriminating about the subscribers they activate," Siber added.
Reducing the rate of churn by one percentage point can add some $150 million to the valuation of the average mobile operator, the study said.
The study said "churn" -- the rate at which customers are lost -- was at "epidemic proportions" with annual rates averaging 30 percent in the United States and 25 percent in Europe.
It said churn cost U.S. and European companies over $4.0 billion each year and rates could top 40 percent if operators continue to chase marginal customers.
Companies were urged to invest in retention, targeting corporate customers through improved service and better account management. Over 80 percent of revenues are generated by retained customers.
A large proportion - 40 percent - of 'churn' actually involves customers switching between packages offered by the same carrier. Dealers often encourage this in order to secure incentive rewards.
The practice hurts operators as a new subscriber can cost up to $400 in handset subsidies, commission and marketing.
